extracted.intended_audience: aspiring stand-up comedians, joke writers, and performers learning Greg Dean's system
extracted.subtask_description: Producing stand-up-joke material using Greg Dean's Joke Prospector system: construct setups that create a target assumption around a connector, then craft a punch that forces a surprising but hindsight-logical reinterpretation; use POV/act-outs and performance techniques to deliver material effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear setup establishing a target assumption
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there a clear setup that establishes a target assumption?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The setup should lead the audience to make a Target Assumption — the obvious/expected interpretation of the connector. A good setup subtly guides the audience toward the intended assumption without telegraphing the punch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence of a connector (two-meaning element)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there a connector — an element with two valid interpretations?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The connector is the 'magical element' around which the joke is built. It must legitimately support both the expected interpretation (target assumption) and an alternative reinterpretation. Without a true dual-meaning connector, the joke structure fails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punch forces a reinterpretation of the connector
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the punchline force a reinterpretation of the connector?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The punch (punchline) must force the audience to reinterpret the connector so they see the alternate, simultaneous meaning. The punch is the mechanism that flips the audience from the target assumption to the reinterpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinterpretation is surprising yet logical in hindsight
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the reinterpretation surprising yet logical in hindsight?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The best reinterpreations are unexpected at the moment of reveal but make sense once seen — audience members should feel the laugh comes from recognizing a plausible second meaning, not from a non-sequitur. Surprise + retrospective logic is the intended effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of POVs / act outs in performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Are POVs (act outs) used effectively if performance is involved?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dean teaches 'act outs' — quick scenes comics act out during a routine — and explains three POVs inside a scene as fundamental tools. Effective POV shifting uses stage movement and facial direction changes to sell the scene and heighten the reinterpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core joke components (setup, connector, target assumption, reinterpretation, punch)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the joke include the core components: Setup, Connector, Target Assumption, Reinterpretation, Punch?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A complete Joke Prospector structure explicitly or implicitly contains these elements: Setup (leads to target assumption); Connector (word/element with two meanings); Target Assumption (expected meaning); Reinterpretation (surprising second meaning); Punch (line that forces reinterpretation). When analyzing or constructing jokes, identify each component.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding and applying the Three POVs
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the three POVs inside a scene understood and applied to maximize act out effectiveness?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dean emphasizes three POVs within a scene as the basis for why act outs are funny. Use POV awareness to choose where to stand, where to look, and which character to embody; shifting POVs deliberately can reveal the reinterpretation more dramatically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five Mechanisms explanation of why jokes work
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the material reflect understanding or application of Dean's '5 Mechanisms' that explain how jokes produce laughter?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dean's system includes '5 Mechanisms' that reveal exactly how jokes work. While the summary does not enumerate them, the rubric implies using these mechanisms (e.g., connector/reinterpretation mechanics) when diagnosing or crafting jokes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routine construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the material organized into a coherent routine with effective ordering and transitions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book addresses routine construction; evaluate whether jokes flow, build momentum, and are ordered to maximize audience response. Consider tag placement, callbacks, and how setups lead into one another.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rehearsal techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Are rehearsal and practice methods applied to tighten timing and delivery?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dean covers rehearsal techniques. Assess whether the performer has rehearsed physicality, timing, and line delivery; whether pacing has been refined to maximize the punch's impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microphone handling and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Is microphone technique and comedic timing appropriate to enhance the joke?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Microphone handling and precise timing affect how a connector and punch land. Check for distractions from poor mic technique and whether pauses/beat timing enhance the reinterpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heckler management
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the performer manage hecklers in a way that preserves or enhances material?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dean's coverage includes heckler management; evaluate whether the performer defuses disruptions without derailing the joke structure or uses them opportunistically while maintaining control and momentum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material refinement
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the joke material refined through iteration to tighten setup, connector clarity, and punch impact?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material refinement involves testing, cutting unnecessary words, sharpening the connector, and ensuring the reinterpretation is the strongest, clearest surprise possible. Assess whether the joke has undergone such refinement.
